title: The site is down
briefing: Welcome to app-01 — the server that runs the website. You're on call.
The site is throwing 'connection refused'. The web server, nginx, is a
background service (a daemon). Services are managed with systemctl.
tips: See a service's state with: systemctl status nginx.
'active' means running now. Starting a service needs privilege — use sudo.
objective: Bring the nginx web service back up so it is active (running).
expert_objective: app-01: the web tier is down. Restore it.
hints: First look: `systemctl status nginx`. The Active line will say 'inactive (dead)'.
Start it. Changing a service needs root, so prefix with sudo: `sudo systemctl start nginx`.
`sudo systemctl start nginx`, then confirm with `systemctl status nginx` (Active: active (running)).
solution:
systemctl status nginx
sudo systemctl start nginx
explanation: systemctl is how you drive the services running on a modern Linux box. `status` inspects one, `start` brings it up. Because a stopped service affects everyone on the machine, starting it needs root — that's what sudo is for.
